interventions.name: Introduce legume-based cover crops
interventions.mechanism: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen and their root exudates feed soil microbial communities, increasing organic matter turnover and microbial biomass.

secondary_effects.estimate: moderate increase if flowering legumes are used

interventions.reference: FAO, Conservation Agriculture and Soil Carbon Sequestration Report (2017)

interventions.name: Convert monoculture to agroforestry or intercropping
interventions.mechanism: Tree-crop integration adds vertical habitat structure, reduces soil surface temperature and evaporation, and creates microhabitats that support a wider range of insects and birds.

secondary_effects.estimate: up to 60% higher than adjacent monoculture, per comparative studies

interventions.reference: Torralba et al., Agroforestry and biodiversity: a meta-analysis, Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment (2016)

interventions.name: Establish native riparian buffer strips along water channels
interventions.mechanism: Vegetated buffer strips filter agrochemical runoff before it reaches waterways and provide continuous habitat corridors that counteract fragmentation.

primary_effect.estimate: -30-50% nutrient runoff into adjacent water bodies

interventions.reference: Stutter et al., Vegetated buffer strips and their function on agricultural runoff, Journal of Environmental Quality (2012)

interventions.name: Shift to reduced or no-till cultivation
interventions.mechanism: Minimizing soil disturbance preserves fungal networks and soil structure, slowing organic carbon oxidation and reducing erosion.

secondary_effects.estimate: increased fungal to bacterial ratio, associated with more stable soil aggregates

interventions.reference: Lal, Soil carbon sequestration impacts on global climate change and food security, Science (2004)

interventions.name: Plant wildflower or pollinator habitat strips at field margins
interventions.mechanism: Field-margin flowering strips provide nectar and nesting resources that are otherwise absent in monoculture landscapes, directly supplementing pollinator populations.

primary_effect.estimate: up to 2x visitation rate within 1-2 seasons

interventions.reference: Scheper et al., Environmental factors driving the effectiveness of European agri-environmental measures, Ecology Letters (2013)

interventions.name: Assisted natural regeneration of degraded forest patches
interventions.mechanism: Protecting and lightly managing existing seed sources and root stock allows forest cover to recover faster than active replanting, at lower cost and with locally adapted species composition.

primary_effect.estimate: measurable canopy cover recovery within 5-10 years

secondary_effects.estimate: potential local microclimate stabilization at landscape scale

interventions.reference: Chazdon & Guariguata, Natural regeneration as a tool for large-scale forest restoration, Biotropica (2016)
